text: For the choirmaster. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
I said, "I will watch my ways so I do not sin with my tongue; I will keep a muzzle on my mouth as long as the wicked are before me."
I was mute in silence; I kept still, even from good, and my pain grew worse.

versions.text: I was mute and silent; I held back even from good, and my pain was stirred up.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew דוּמִיָּה is a noun in adverbial position ("in silence"), and נֶעְכָּר conveys that the pain was stirred up/worsened. "My pain grew worse" reads more naturally aloud and better captures the intensification.

text: My heart grew hot within me; as I mused, the fire burned. Then I spoke with my tongue:
"Show me, LORD, my end and what the measure of my days is; let me know how fleeting I am.
You have made my days mere handbreadths; my lifetime is as nothing before you. Surely everyone stands as a breath. Selah
Surely everyone walks about as a mere shadow; surely for nothing they bustle about; they heap up wealth and do not know who will gather it.

versions.text: Surely a man walks about as a shadow; surely for nothing they are in turmoil; he heaps up wealth and does not know who will gather it.
versions.explanation: The verse mixes singular ("a man... he") and plural ("they") awkwardly. Making number consistent improves oral flow. Also "heaps up wealth" adds a word not in Hebrew (יִצְבֹּר is simply "heaps up"); consider a footnote noting "wealth" is implied.

text: And now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you.
Deliver me from all my transgressions; do not make me the scorn of fools.
I am silent; I do not open my mouth, for you are the one who has done it.
Remove your plague from me; I am consumed by the hostility of your hand.

versions.text: Remove your affliction from me; I am worn out by the blow of your hand.
versions.explanation: נֶגַע is more concretely "plague/stroke," and כָלִיתִי means "I am consumed/finished," stronger than "worn out." תִּגְרַת denotes assault or hostility rather than a single blow.

text: When you discipline a man with rebukes for sin, you consume like a moth what he treasures. Surely everyone is but a breath. Selah
Hear my prayer, LORD, and listen to my cry for help; do not be silent at my tears. For I am a stranger with you, a sojourner, like all my fathers.
Look away from me, that I may find relief, before I depart and am no more."

versions.text: Look away from me, that I may smile again, before I depart and am no more."
versions.explanation: אַבְלִיגָה means to brighten up or recover cheer; "find relief" or "be glad again" is closer to the sense of recovery from the affliction described, and "smile again" risks sounding overly modern in oral reading.
